title: CSS Quantum LRCs with Intersecting Recovery Sets: Constructions and Bounds
authors: Evagoras Stylianou, Vinayak Ramkumar, Holger Boche, Rawad Bitar
abstract: In this work, we study $(r,t,x)$ quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) with locality $r$, $t$ recovery sets per qudit, and intersection parameter $x$. We first show that, assuming the underlying classical codes have dual minimum distance at least two, a CSS code is an $(r,t,x)$-qLRC if and only if the underlying classical codes are $(r,t,x)$ classical LRCs (cLRCs) with common recovery sets. We then use subset-inclusion matrices to construct families of binary dual-containing $(r,t,x)$-cLRCs, which yield binary $(r,t,x)$-qLRCs via the CSS construction. For CSS $(r,t,x)$-qLRCs, we derive upper bounds on the dimension and rate, minimum-distance bounds in the pure case, and a Singleton-like dimension bound in the exact case. Finally, we show that these families attain high rates and nontrivial minimum distances.
summary: This paper develops the theory and explicit constructions for Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes (qLRCs) characterized by parameters $(r, t, x)$. It shows that these quantum codes can be derived from classical LRCs via the CSS construction. The main contribution is deriving tight upper bounds on the code rate and dimension, alongside providing concrete families of such codes.
main_problem: The work focuses on constructing and deriving bounds for quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) with specific parameters $(r, t, x)$. It establishes the necessary and sufficient conditions for a CSS code to achieve this structure.
main_result: Explicit families of binary dual-containing classical LRCs are constructed using subset-inclusion matrices, which yield corresponding quantum qLRCs. Upper bounds on the dimension and rate for these codes are derived.
method: The authors utilize the CSS construction to translate known results from classical locally recoverable codes (cLRCs) into the quantum domain. They derive bounds by analyzing puncturing techniques applied to the underlying classical code structure.
model_or_system: The model is Quantum Error Correction, specifically focusing on $(r, t, x)$-qLRCs built via the CSS construction from binary linear codes $C$. The parameters involve locality ($r$), availability ($t$), and intersection parameter ($x$).
key_observables: Code dimension ($\kappa$), code rate (R), minimum distance ($\delta$), and the specific parameters $(r, t, x)$.
important_parameters: Locality $r$, availability $t$, intersection parameter $x$, and the underlying classical code structure defined by parameters $(m, s, \alpha)$ in the construction.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption for the necessary and sufficient condition is that the underlying classical codes have a dual minimum distance of at least two. The constructions also rely on the resulting classical code being dual-containing.
figures_summary: TABLE I lists representative parameters $(m, s, \alpha)$ satisfying the required conditions and provides the corresponding quantum code parameters $[[n, \kappa, \delta]]_q$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the equivalence between CSS qLRCs and cLRCs (Theorem 1). It then details a construction method using subset-inclusion matrices to generate explicit cLRCs. Finally, it derives general upper bounds and specific Singleton-like dimension bounds for the resulting quantum codes.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools and concrete constructions for advanced quantum error correcting codes that go beyond standard stabilizer or distance-based requirements by incorporating locality constraints.
